heroSubtitle: Stabilised GHRH(1-44) analogue — long-acting GHRH-receptor agonist for GH-axis research
description: Tesamorelin is a 44-amino-acid GHRH analogue: the full-length GHRH(1-44) sequence with a trans-3-hexenoyl modification at the N-terminus that increases resistance to DPP-IV cleavage. That stability difference is the reason it is used in GH-axis research where a longer-acting GHRH-receptor stimulus is required, as distinct from the shorter GHRH(1-29) analogue Sermorelin.

faq.question: What is Tesamorelin?
faq.answer: Tesamorelin (CAS 218949-48-5) is a stabilised GHRH(1-44) analogue used as a research reagent in growth-hormone-axis studies.

faq.question: How does it differ from Sermorelin?
faq.answer: Sermorelin is GHRH(1-29); Tesamorelin is the full-length GHRH(1-44) with an N-terminal modification that slows enzymatic degradation, so research designs differ in the duration of receptor stimulation.

faq.question: Which kit sizes are available?
faq.answer: 5 mg, 10 mg and 20 mg × 10-vial kits — the widest configuration range in our GH-axis portfolio.

faq.question: Do you supply research documentation?
faq.answer: Yes: batch-specific COA, and MS/HPLC data on request. Our documentation is analytical, not regulatory — these are research reagents.
